title: `any` stays usable in authored .sm: the language does not forbid it
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Dynamic Features': '`any` and `eval` remain usable. General Smithers guidance may lint against them; the language does not forbid them.' The correct observable behavior is that the program compiles and runs — a compiler that rejected `any` outright would fail this case, and specification/compatibility.mdx §4 forbids invalidating TypeScript escape hatches. WITHDRAWAL (2026-08-23): this case previously pinned the second bucket of the portable / `TypeScript`-required / forbidden classification, citing 'Use of any and eval MUST contribute TypeScript.' That classification and the `TypeScript` requirement are withdrawn — 'There is no portable / `TypeScript`-required / forbidden classification, because there is no second target to be portable to' — so the case now pins only the half of the old sentence the specification kept: `any` is not forbidden. The observable is unchanged; only the citation moved.
